results.title: What Is Google TurboQuant? The KV Cache Compression That ...
results.content: In late 2024, Google DeepMind introduced TurboQuant — a KV cache compression algorithm that squeezes memory usage down to 3 bits per value with essentially zero accuracy loss. The result: up to 8x faster inference and 6x reduction in memory consumption on H100 GPUs. When that news landed, Micron and SK Hynix saw their stock prices drop sharply. Investors realized that the industry’s assumption — more AI means more memory demand — had just gotten significantly more complicated. [...] Per-head calibration. Rather than applying a single global quantization scheme across the entire KV cache, TurboQuant calibrates quantization parameters independently for each attention head. Different heads have different value distributions, and treating them uniformly wastes precision where it matters. [...] Google’s research claims accuracy that is statistically indistinguishable from full-precision KV cache on standard benchmarks, including long-context tasks. However, “zero accuracy loss” in this context means performance within the margin of error on the specific benchmarks tested, not a mathematical guarantee. Results may vary slightly depending on the task, model size, and context type. Independent replication of the benchmarks is still in early stages.

   _KV cache compression shifts the build-vs-buy math for on-premise inference. Enterprises with data residency requirements should evaluate this now._

On March 25, Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron stock prices fell . The trigger: a blog post from Google Research about data compression. When investors get nervous about a compression algorithm, infrastructure leaders should pay attention. [...] TurboQuant is not the only KV cache method. NVIDIA’s KVTC (KV Cache Transform Coding), also presented at ICLR 2026, achieves up to 20x compression at less than 1 percentage point of accuracy loss — tested on models from 1.5B to 70B, a significantly broader range than TurboQuant’s benchmarks. KVTC requires calibration data and integrates into NVIDIA’s Dynamo framework with vLLM compatibility. The tradeoff: TurboQuant’s data-oblivious simplicity (immediately deployable, no calibration overhead) [...] Local AI inference does not fail because of model quality. It fails because of memory. TurboQuant proves that this bottleneck was never fundamental. It was an engineering problem, and it now has a mathematically near-optimal solution.

Near-zero accuracy loss at 6x KV cache compression. No training required. Independently validated by numerous community reimplementations on at least five different platforms, working from the paper alone, without any code from Google.
